domain_title: Accountability, evidence, risk decisions and lifecycle governance
title: Calendar-driven or ambiguous governance decisions
canonical_definition: Progress depends on periodic forums, silent assent or unclear authority, or automated recommendations are mistaken for approval.

conditions: Every governed lifecycle transition, exception, residual-risk acceptance and material escalation.
Record the assessed release, operating scope and evidence that supports any applicability decision.

primary_questions.question: Does the case exhibit Calendar-driven or ambiguous governance decisions: Progress depends on periodic forums, silent assent or unclear authority, or automated recommendations are mistaken for approval.
Do implemented workflows, data paths or operations show green output treated as authorization, silence counted as approval, or untracked approval conditions?
Does current evidence test presence or scoped absence of Calendar-driven or ambiguous governance decisions, or does it remain unknown?

antipattern_indicators: Routine decisions wait for a monthly forum
Green output is treated as authorization

conditions: Refer verified calendar-driven or ambiguous governance decisions to the accountable authority before progression where the condition materially affects the requested operating scope.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1, GOVERN 2.1 (PDF p. 28), GOVERN 2.3 (PDF p. 28), MANAGE 1.1 (PDF p. 37)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: The voluntary framework provides guidance on assigning decision responsibility and evaluating whether development or deployment should proceed. The SAE criteria define the object-specific rules. Confirm any binding obligation through the accountable authority and its applicable source.

failure_mechanism: The declared or implemented control can be unreliable where a decision depends on implied assent, calendar status or an automated recommendation. The mechanism can have an operational effect where a workflow advanced with a missing approval, expired delegation or unverified condition.
potential_consequences: An initiative may advance without an accountable authorization or required controls.

atomic_tests.test: Compare the effective governance and design records. Determine whether a decision depends on implied assent, calendar status or an automated recommendation. Identify the system scope and the record that supports each conclusion.

Trace actual configurations or activity for the assessed release. Determine whether a workflow advanced with a missing approval, expired delegation or unverified condition. Attribute each observation to the specific path, time and decision.

Independently review trace sampled transitions and exceptions from request to disposition, confirming decision authority, evidence and timing. Record whether each material mechanism was tested, the observed result and the scope limitations.

required_evidence.title: Effective design and governance records
required_evidence.description: Review the versioned owner decision and relevant specifications for evidence of whether a decision depends on implied assent, calendar status or an automated recommendation. Preserve material conflict and applicability context.

required_evidence.title: Observed condition or enforcement trace
required_evidence.description: Use effective configuration or dated operational records to determine whether a workflow advanced with a missing approval, expired delegation or unverified condition. Identify the version, affected paths and period represented.

required_evidence.title: Executed scoped comparison
required_evidence.description: Provide trace sampled transitions and exceptions from request to disposition, confirming decision authority, evidence and timing. Include current scope, expected results, observed results, retained evidence and unresolved cases.

required_evidence.title: Independent review and limitations
required_evidence.description: An independent reviewer confirms the assessed version, completeness of coverage, result, limitations and whether a material change requires a new test.

required_artifacts: Trace sampled transitions and exceptions from request to disposition, confirming decision authority, evidence and timing.
Current version and scope with all material failure paths and cases identified.
Expected and observed results, attributable records, and independent review of coverage and residual limitations.

sufficiency: Presence requires affirmative evidence for a material mechanism. Examine whether a decision depends on implied assent, calendar status or an automated recommendation, and separately check whether a workflow advanced with a missing approval, expired delegation or unverified condition. A supported mechanism may establish presence within its evidenced scope.
Keep unresolved or contradictory mechanisms UNKNOWN and preserve the competing records. Refer material interpretation conflicts to the accountable human authority.

Use TESTED_ABSENT only after a current, executed, successful and independently verified evaluation covers all material paths within scope. Use trace sampled transitions and exceptions from request to disposition, confirming decision authority, evidence and timing. Reassess when material changes affect that scope.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: A document can identify a declared gap. Effective configuration can demonstrate a reachable condition. Observed records support only their covered period and workflow. TESTED_ABSENT requires the complete scoped absence contract.
false_positive_guards: A pre-authorized delegation is valid only within an explicit scope and period with an attributable decision record.
Confirm that the observed or alleged condition applies to the current assessed release and a reachable path.
prohibited_inferences: A gap or UNKNOWN in F4 alone cannot establish AP-F4 presence.
Missing complaints, incident silence and unsuccessful collection cannot establish absence.
Model output and tactic selection grant no authority to approve, close a finding or accept risk.

finding_definitions.title: Design or intent shows calendar-driven or ambiguous governance decisions
Implementation or operating evidence shows calendar-driven or ambiguous governance decisions
Presence or tested absence of calendar-driven or ambiguous governance decisions is unresolved within scope
